title: Choropleth map
description: Regions on a real map, shaded by their value in steps. Use when: Where is it high and where is it low: a rate or average per country, state or province, where the geographic pattern is the message. Avoid when: The values are totals that grow with area or population (large regions look heavier), or every region must be equally visible (use tileMap)

region.description: Region name or code, matched to a region of options.map (string)

map.description: Map. "auto" picks the registered map that matches the most region values. "world" is 177 countries (Natural Earth 1:110m, de facto borders; ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes, English and common names), "us-states" is the 50 US states and DC with Alaska and Hawaii moved below (postal codes, FIPS codes, names), "kr-sido" is South Korea's 16 first-level regions from 2026-07-01. Or a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of Polygon and MultiPolygon features in longitude and latitude degrees. ztd-charts/server, the CLI and the MCP server load every built-in map; in the browser import the map from ztd-charts/geo/<name> and pass it to registerMap

focus.description: Show only part of the world map, cropped and enlarged. Countries of other regions inside the frame are drawn pale and take no data. Regions follow UN M49

featureId.description: GeoJSON property that holds the region id. Without it: feature.id, then the id or code property

featureName.description: GeoJSON property that holds the region name. Without it: the name or NAME property

legend.description: Show the color legend. It also shows a No data swatch when some regions have no value

legendLabels.description: Names at both ends of the legend

colorReverse.description: Darkest color for the smallest value, for rankings where 1st should stand out. The default highlight moves to the smallest value too

colorCenter.description: Value that gets the lightest color. Values above take the accent color and values below take gray, so gains and losses split there (for example 0)

colorSteps.description: Number of color steps. The legend shows each step, and hovering a step leaves only its regions

ranking.description: Ranked list of the highest and lowest regions beside the map. "auto" shows it when the chart is at least 600px wide

labels.description: Language of region names on the Korean map. "auto" uses Korean names when a matched region value contains Hangul, otherwise the locale's language

height.description: Height in px. Without it, each chart picks a default that fits its width

width.description: Fixed width in px. Without it, the chart fits its parent

highlight.description: Item to highlight. An index, a name, an array, or "max" | "min" | "first" | "last" | "none"

format.description: Value format. "number" | "integer" | "percent" (values are already percents: 42 → "42%") | "ratio" (0.42 → "42%") | "compact" | "currency" (KRW for Korean locales, otherwise USD; for another currency pass Intl options with currency) | "decimal" or Intl.NumberFormat options

anyOf.description: Intl.NumberFormat options plus suffix and prefix

unit.description: Unit appended to values. For example "%" or "ms"

locale.description: Locale for numbers, dates and the text a chart writes itself (tooltips, screen reader sentences). "ko" or "ko-*" switches to Korean. Falls back to the ThemeProvider locale

stagger.description: Delay between items as they enter (ms)

reducedMotion.description: "auto" follows the OS setting. true always turns motion off

animateOnView.description: Play when the chart scrolls into view

showLabels.description: Labels drawn on the chart (values and names)

syncId.description: Charts with the same syncId show the hovered x together (line, area, bar, candlestick). <ChartGrid sync> sets one for every chart inside it

description.description: Description for screen readers. Built from the data when omitted

tooltip.description: Show tooltips. { template: "{label} · {value} · owner {owner}" } writes them: {label}, {value}, {series} or any other column of the row. \n starts a new line, and a line with an empty value is left out

data.description: An array of objects, or one of { values }, { csv }, { url }

csv.description: CSV text (the first line is the header)

url.description: JSON or CSV address (REST API, Google Sheets CSV export and so on)

select.description: Path to the array inside the response JSON. For example "data.items"

card.description: Wraps the chart in a card with a number, title, legend, one-line takeaway, level badge, source line and download buttons

takeaway.description: Bold one-line takeaway at the bottom

legend.description: "auto" builds the legend from the data. "toggle" also lets viewers click it to show and hide series in the browser (line, area, bar, scatter, and timeline groups). Images and static HTML draw it like "auto"

sample.description: Marks the data as sample data

source.description: Source line under the chart, after "Source: "

note.description: Note on the same line, such as the as-of date

accent.description: A word of the title to color with the accent color, used instead of a legend

download.description: Download buttons in the browser: true for CSV, SVG and PNG, or a list. Not drawn in SVG, PNG or static HTML
